subject: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 1:20 PM PST
Subject: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

Hey Dylan —

As we get closer to wiring the model changelog generator into prod, I want to make sure we’re aligned on how it behaves during control plane RCs + freeze windows.

Key questions from Release Eng:
1) During a code freeze, do we allow customer-visible changelog entries to be published (docs + console feed), or do we queue them until the freeze lifts?
2) If a model metadata change event happens during RC (e.g., deprecation date set, compatibility note clarified), can the generator still produce drafts + run validation, but defer publish?
3) What’s the “emergency path” if we need to correct wording post-publish (audit-safe supersede vs edit-in-place)?

Proposed default from my side: keep generating drafts during freeze; only publish if tagged as “release-note-only” (no runtime/control-plane deploy required) and approved by the usual reviewers.

Can we do 20 min this week to lock down the policy and bake it into the runbook?

- Connor
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 2:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

Connor —

Agree we need to formalize this.

How we currently treat freeze windows (control plane):
- Code freeze typically starts when we cut the RC (Mon ~5pm PT) and ends after production promote (Thu morning PT).
- We still allow “data/config” changes that are reversible and don’t require a deploy, but we want explicit on-call awareness.

Where I think changelog publish fits:
- Generator producing drafts + validation: should always be allowed (it’s internal + reduces post-freeze backlog).
- Publishing customer-facing entries: allowed during freeze IF (a) no deploy is required for the publish path, and (b) it does not impact request serving.

The one caveat: if the publish step touches console/backend in a way that requires a deploy (new routes, schema change), it should be blocked like any other production change.

For corrections post-publish: we should not edit-in-place. Supersede with a corrected entry and keep the original for audit. (I believe that’s already in scope.)

If you want to loop in Marissa/Elliot for product/docs expectations, go for it.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Sponsor, Model Catalog + Control Plane


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 2:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

Looping in Marissa + Elliot for quick alignment.

Dylan — makes sense. The main ambiguity for us is whether “docs publish” is truly deploy-less. We’re planning on the docs site consuming the published feed and generating pages (plus RSS) as part of the docs pipeline.

What I’d like to propose as policy text (happy to adjust):

During RC/freeze:
- Continue consuming model change-events and generating drafts.
- Allow approvals (draft -> in_review -> approved) as normal.
- Publish is allowed only if:
  1) the change is content-only and does not require a control plane/runtime deploy, AND
  2) release engineering on-call acknowledges (Slack reaction / lightweight ticket), AND
  3) the entry includes compatibility notes (template requirement).

Blocked during RC/freeze:
- Any publish path that requires deploying console/control-plane services.
- Any schema migration that changes validation behavior in prod.

Open question for Elliot: can the docs output be updated from the feed without merging/deploying redwood-docs during our freeze?

Also: we should define the backpressure behavior. If we’re not publishing for ~72 hours, console could show “pending publication” entries internally, but customers shouldn’t see partials.

- Connor


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 3:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

Thanks for looping me in.

From a product/customer standpoint:
- We should optimize for customers seeing release notes close to when behavior/availability changes.
- That said, I’m fine with a short delay during RC/freeze as long as it’s consistent and we can explain it.

Two requests:
1) If we do defer publish, can we make sure Support has access to the “pending” draft so they can answer questions if a customer notices something?
2) If the entry is a deprecation notice (sunset date / replacement), I’d prefer we do NOT delay publishing it until the freeze lifts. Those are change-management heavy and enterprises will ask why the notice is late.

So maybe the policy has exceptions for:
- Deprecations/sunsets
- Security/policy notes (if we’re tightening behavior)

Otherwise, your “drafts always / publish sometimes” approach sounds good.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Console & Rollouts

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 4:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

On docs:

Our current plan (matches redwood-docs PR direction) is:
- The public docs site pulls from the published changelog feed and renders release note pages on a scheduled job.
- For the actual “release notes content,” we do not need to merge/deploy redwood-docs every time. That’s the main reason we went with feed-driven generation.

So, content publish during a control plane freeze is fine from the docs side.

Caveats:
- If we’re changing the templates/lint rules, or the navigation/IA, that’s still a docs deploy (and should be treated like a normal change).
- Please keep the “no internal-only fields” guardrails on; if we’re publishing during freeze, we need to be confident the redaction/lint checks are already in place.

Re: Marissa’s request — we can also have an internal-only view of pending drafts in Console (or behind an auth gate) if that’s easier than giving Support direct access to the generator storage.

Elliot
Elliot Price
Docs Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: 
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:21 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

+1 to carving out deprecations as “always publish” (still with approval).

One more operational thought: if we’re gating publish during freeze, make sure the pipeline surfaces clear metrics (publish lag, approvals backlog) so we don’t come out of freeze with a pile-up.

Connor — can you incorporate this into the runbook + the release checklist?

- Dylan

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 10:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release train integration: model changelog generator publish behavior during RC/freeze windows

Sounds aligned. I’ll capture as v1 policy text and push into the runbook.

Tentative policy (v1):
- Always generate drafts + run validation.
- Publish allowed during freeze for content-only entries that don’t require deploy.
- Deprecations/sunsets: publish allowed during freeze (with approvals) and require Support-readiness checkbox.
- Corrections: supersede (no edit-in-place) to preserve audit.
- Release Eng on-call acknowledgement required for any publish during freeze (lightweight).
- Observability: publish lag + backlog alerts; we’ll add a “post-freeze drain” checklist item.

Action items:
- Connor: update runbook + release checklist; add a Slack snippet for on-call acknowledgement.
- Elliot: confirm feed-driven publish job schedule and any freeze constraints on the docs infra side.
- Dylan: confirm whether any of the remaining generator/control-plane work will require deploy changes close to GA (so we can schedule outside freeze).

I’ll send a calendar hold for a 20 min check-in early next week to confirm we didn’t miss edge cases.

- Connor
